paper.title: Dynamic recrystallization mechanisms of an Fe–8% Al low density steel under hot rolling conditions
paper.paper_scope: The study investigates the dynamic recrystallization mechanisms of an Fe–8% Al ferritic low-density steel deformed by hot torsion over 900–1100 °C and 0.1–10 s−1, showing that a competition between continuous (CDRX) and discontinuous (DDRX) dynamic recrystallization governs the resulting microstructure and texture depending on strain, strain rate and temperature.

alloys.description: Hot-rolled ferritic iron–aluminium low-density steel supplied by ArcelorMittal Maizières and rolled in three successive passes (cumulative deformation ~1). The material is 100% recrystallized with an initial equiaxed grain size of ~800 µm and is morphologically isotropic.
alloys.alloys_notes: Composition taken from Table 1 given in 10^-3 wt.%: Al 8150, Mn 100, C 8.6, Ti+Nb+V <100, Fe balance. The alloy is a ferritic A2 (non-ordered) solid solution; the ~8% Al gives a density of ~7 g cm−3 (~10% density reduction vs conventional steels). No atomic percent reported.

unmapped_findings: Two types of dynamic recrystallization operate in this Fe–8% Al ferritic steel during hot deformation: DDRX at high temperature and high strain rate (1100 °C, 5–10 s−1), and CDRX at lower temperature and strain rate (e.g. 1000 °C, 0.1 s−1), with a competition between the two mechanisms depending on deformation conditions.

The recrystallized grains formed by DDRX have no preferred orientation (very low texture intensity), whereas CDRX produces a well-defined torsion texture with the strongest D2: −112<111> component (self-symmetric), maximal at ε = 15.

Geometric dynamic recrystallization (GDRX) is discussed as an additional mechanism associated with pre-existing high angle boundaries, serrations and pinch-off at large strain, possibly operating simultaneously with CDRX.

The initial 100% recrystallized ferritic Fe–8% Al has a ~800 µm equiaxed grain size; all torsion samples were quenched (0.5 s with argon, cooling rate ~200 °C s−1) after deformation to avoid post-dynamic recrystallization.
To limit the roping surface defect (attributed to inhomogeneous grain orientation), favouring DDRX during hot rolling to obtain randomly oriented recrystallized grains is suggested as advantageous.
